prompt: What is the writer asking the team to do by saying ‘Please leave room for the people who remember it’?
promptZh: 文中說「請也顧及那些還記得這首曲子的人」時，寫信者要節目小組怎麼做？

options.text: Describe the original music as a premiere but mention that an earlier rehearsal was closed to visitors.
options.zh: 把原本的樂曲稱作首演，同時提到先前的排練並未開放訪客。
options.whyZh: 不公開的排練不妨礙這個新版本首演，但原有曲子去年已公開演奏過，不能把原曲稱為首演。

options.text: Recognize the earlier concert and present the five-player arrangement, rather than the tune, as a premiere.
options.zh: 提及先前的音樂會，並把五人改編版而非原曲稱為首演。
options.whyZh: 觀眾可能記得去年公開演過的曲調；五人版本則只有不公開的排練，這次才是該改編版本首次公開演出。

options.text: Advertise only familiar music, since listeners have already heard the complete five-player arrangement.
options.zh: 只宣傳大家熟悉的樂曲，因為聽眾已聽過完整五人改編版。
options.whyZh: 大家可能聽過的是早期三重奏版；完整的五人版只在不公開的排練裡演過。

options.text: Drop the word ‘premiere’ altogether because the five players have already performed the whole score once.
options.zh: 完全不用「首演」一詞，因為那五位樂手已完整演奏過一次。
options.whyZh: 是否完整演奏不是關鍵；規則看的是這個版本是否曾公開演出，不公開的排練不算。

explanationZh: 觀眾可能記得去年公開演過的曲調；五人版本則只有不公開的排練，這次才是該改編版本首次公開演出。

vocabulary.note: 改編版未曾公開演出，與旋律本身曾公開演過並不衝突。

evidence: When we describe a first performance, be clear about what is new. A piece of music and an arrangement of that piece are not the same thing: an arrangement changes how the music is played, although the original tune remains. We should name a previous public performance if it helps readers understand why the tune may sound familiar. We can call an arrangement a premiere only if that particular arrangement has never been performed in public. / People may remember Under the Lantern from last year’s library concert, where our trio played it. Our conductor has since written a five-player arrangement. The five of us played through its full score in a rehearsal closed to visitors; the version has not been heard at any public event. I know someone has already drafted the headline ‘A tune you’ve never heard’ for the programme. Please leave room for the people who remember it.

evidenceSpans.exactQuote: When we describe a first performance, be clear about what is new. A piece of music and an arrangement of that piece are not the same thing: an arrangement changes how the music is played, although the original tune remains. We should name a previous public performance if it helps readers understand why the tune may sound familiar. We can call an arrangement a premiere only if that particular arrangement has never been performed in public.

People may remember Under the Lantern from last year’s library concert, where our trio played it. Our conductor has since written a five-player arrangement. The five of us played through its full score in a rehearsal closed to visitors; the version has not been heard at any public event. I know someone has already drafted the headline ‘A tune you’ve never heard’ for the programme. Please leave room for the people who remember it.
